headline: Highest risk is data leakage from plano’s broad egress and API/file surfaces; dagster appears local-only, limiting injection and conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection bridge is not documented: dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, MCP, or network egress, while plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible API and config file surface. The only plausible pathway is unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so blast radius is small and interaction is weakly evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies plano output into dagster-managed content
IF an external orchestrator bridges plano API responses into dagster inputs
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workflows
Disable manual copy-paste between outputs and inputs
Add a review step before any content is reused
Use distinct workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging across the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster is local-only and touches no declared data classes, but plano has broad network egress and handles logs, traces, and metrics. If dagster-managed artifacts are forwarded into plano’s API path, sensitive operational data can leave the local boundary in default-like deployments. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF dagster outputs are sent into plano’s OpenAI-compatible endpoint
IF logs or traces from plano include content derived from dagster artifacts
mitigations: Do not route dagster outputs into plano by default
Redact logs, traces, and metrics before forwarding
Use separate credentials and tenants
Restrict plano egress to approved destinations
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the gateway

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git, or egress network, while plano exposes only broad egress and a config file surface. There is no documented overlapping write authority to the same mutable resource, so a true capability conflict is unlikely. Any conflict would require an external shared target not present in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable API or datastore
IF an orchestrator grants dagster write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate mutable resources to each agent
Avoid concurrent writes to shared configs
Serialize any updates through one controller
Audit for hidden shared credentials
requires-engineering: add locking around shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plano can act as an API gateway and dagster can produce pipeline outputs, so a plausible cascade exists if plano treats dagster-generated content as authoritative. Dagster has no built-in verification or downstream action authority shown, but plano’s routing role makes misclassification or unverified propagation a realistic default risk. Uncertainty remains because the exact integration is undocumented.
conditions: IF plano forwards dagster-produced content without validation
IF downstream systems trust plano-routed outputs as facts
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on dagster outputs
Mark dagster outputs as untrusted metadata
Log and review any transformed payloads
requires-engineering: implement confidence/provenance propagation

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is declared for either agent, and both profiles are docs-only/open-source with no stated residency or retention mismatch. The only compliance concern is a generic logging/telemetry mismatch around plano’s logs, traces, and metrics, but the evidence is too thin for medium severity. Dagster is not cited beyond its lack of declared data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through plano’s logs, traces, or metrics
IF a deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not configured here
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Set short retention on logs and traces
Document data-class handling for both agents
Review residency requirements before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and residency
